dw.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
dw.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

dw.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
dw.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

dw.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
dw.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. dw.context: Darcy-Weisbach friction factor. Dimensionless coefficient in the Darcy-Weisbach head loss equation. Distinct from Hazen-Williams C coefficient.
dw.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term. In some languages, 'friction' and 'resistance' terms compete — prefer 'friction' to match the Darcy-Weisbach naming convention. Kept dw_friction_factor unchanged and standardized the glossary to 'د اصطکاک فاکتور' to match established incumbent usage, same defect class as the km fix above. dw.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
dw.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

dw.context: Flow regime in which fluid moves in parallel layers with no lateral mixing. Reynolds number below ~2000. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach calculator flow regime check.
dw.translation_notes: Nearly always a direct cognate or borrowing from the Latin in technical languages. Confirm the local engineering convention.

dw.context: Flow regime between laminar and turbulent — Reynolds number roughly 2000–4000. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach calculator flow regime check.
dw.translation_notes: Use the adjective form meaning 'between two states'. Some languages use 'critical flow' for this regime — check local hydraulics convention.

dw.context: Flow regime with chaotic, irregular mixing. Reynolds number above ~4000. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach calculator flow regime check.
dw.translation_notes: Nearly always a cognate. Some languages distinguish 'turbulent' (adjective) from 'turbulence' (noun) — use the adjective form.

ip.context: A drip irrigation emitter (dripper/micro-sprinkler) that delivers water at a controlled low flow rate directly to the soil or plant root zone. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the field term most familiar to irrigation practitioners in the target language. Arabic: 'قطارة' (dripper) is the field term, preferred over the academic 'مُصدِر'. Spanish: 'gotero' is field-common in Latin America alongside the technical 'emisor'. Ukrainian: 'крапельниця' is the field term used by irrigation workers. zh CORRECTED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 QA): the wave-2 zh translating agent initially deviated to the generic academic term '灌水器' throughout ip_ keys, reasoning that the calculator's emitter-exponent model (x from ~0 to 0.5) is generic rather than drip-only. Reverted to the established glossary field term '滴头' (dripper) for suite-wide consistency with the ar/es/uk pattern above — this glossary's own policy is field-term-over-academic-generality across all languages, and a generic hydraulic model doesn't change what practitioners actually call the part.

ip.context: Ratio of minimum to average emitter flow rate in a drip or sprinkler system. DU = q_min / q_avg. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the irrigation engineering standard term. 'Uniformity' refers to how evenly water is distributed across the field, not physical evenness of the system. When the source says 'low-quarter DU', see the separate 'low-quarter distribution uniformity' entry. Hebrew: אחידות — never the nonword הוודות (found in shipped he file). Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): tr confirmed on dağılım düzgünlüğü — transliteration+wrong-word forms Uniformluk/Dağıtım were corrected across 7 keys.

ip.context: Irrigation statistic: average of the lowest quarter of measured emitter flows divided by the overall average. Referenced in Irrigation Pressure notes as "textbook low-quarter Distribution Uniformity".
ip.translation_notes: Use the established irrigation-engineering phrase; do not invent one. "Textbook" is an adjective meaning "as defined in standard textbooks" — fr rendered it "manuel" (manual check), wrong. he: uniformity = אחידות, never the nonword הוודות. Wave-1 coinages (2026-07, category-4 sprint): fr="uniformité de distribution du quart inférieur", ro="Uniformitatea Distribuției de sfert inferior", ru="равномерность распределения по нижней четверти", uk="рівномірність розподілу по низькій чверті", bg="равномерност на разпределение по долната четвърт", sr="равномерност расподеле нижег квартила", hr="jednolikost distribucije niske grupe", cs="Uniformita distribuce nízké čtvrtiny", tr="düşük-çeyrek Dağıtım Uniformluğu", id="Keseragaman Distribusi kuartal-bawah". es/pt/it/de already had glossary coverage pre-sprint. Not yet native-reviewed. ur ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 sprint): "نچلی چوتھائی تقسیم یکسانیت" (lower-quarter distribution uniformity) reuses the established ur terms چوتھائی (quarter), تقسیم (distribution), یکسانیت (uniformity, already glossary term for plain "distribution uniformity"). Not yet native-reviewed. hi ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'निम्न-चतुर्थांश वितरण एकरूपता' (low-quarter distribution uniformity) reuses the glossary's own hi="वितरण एकरूपता" for the base "distribution uniformity" term and prefixes "निम्न-चतुर्थांश" (low-quarter), matching the wave-1 pattern of naming the concept literally (fr/ru/uk/id etc.) rather than inventing a new metaphor. NOTE: the hi ip_ file's own pre-sprint text mistakenly used 'पाठ्यपुस्तक' (textbook) where the current English source says 'standard' — corrected to 'मानक' (standard) in lib/lang.ec.hi.php during this sprint; do not reintroduce पाठ्यपुस्तक. ar ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'انتظام التوزيع للربع الأدنى' (uniformity of distribution of the lowest quarter) reuses the glossary's own ar="انتظام التوزيع" base term for plain "distribution uniformity" (switched suite-wide in this sprint from a prior 'توحيد' root to 'انتظام', which better conveys 'evenness' rather than 'unification') and appends 'للربع الأدنى' (of the lowest quarter), naming the concept literally like the fr/ru/uk/id wave-1 coinages. Where the English source's own qualifier 'standard' appears in context (ip_du_estimate, ip_notes_3_def), it is rendered inline as 'القياسي' immediately after this base phrase, kept out of the pure glossary term here for parity with the other languages' entries. bn ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'নিম্ন-চতুর্থাংশ বিতরণ সমতা' (low-quarter distribution uniformity), built on the glossary's own bn="বিতরণ সমতা" base term, naming the concept literally. fa ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'یکنواختی توزیع ربع پایین' (low-quarter distribution uniformity), built on the glossary's own fa="یکنواختی توزیع" base term; where English says "standard" it is rendered inline as "استاندارد" immediately after this base phrase, same pattern as ar. Task 129 STALE-ENGLISH RESYNC (2026-07-21): the ip_ keys ip_du_estimate/ip_q_ratio/ip_notes_3_def (plus ip_worst_case_warn and mhp_notes_2_def) were resynced against the CURRENT English, which was shortened in the Wave-0 reform (commit 7bfbda1) after several languages had already translated the older, longer version. Canonical wording is now 'supply pressure' (NOT the retired 'inlet pressure') and ip_q_ratio's tooltip is ONE short sentence ('This is different than our approximation of the standard uniformity measure.'), not the old separate-check paragraph; mhp_notes_2_def dropped its old '1-3 m/s target range' numeric band. 9 languages carried drift and were rewritten (am, cs, es, hr, km, pt, ru, tr, uk); the other 17 already reflected current English. es/hi also had 'textbook'->'standard' aligned (Tom: negligible/synonymic, not swept elsewhere).

ip.context: Depth of water applied per unit time by a drip or sprinkler system. PR = q / A_e. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: In irrigation, 'application rate' or 'precipitation rate' (for sprinklers) or 'irrigation rate'. Use the field irrigation term. Do not use a water-quality or chemical-application connotation. Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): hi 'सिंचाई दर' (irrigation rate) drift standardized to file-dominant अनुप्रयोग term (ip_pr='अनुप्रयोग दर'); am confirmed on ልፍፍ.

ip.context: Irrigation branch line carrying emitters, fed by the mainline. Pairs with "mainline". Appears throughout Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: Branch pipe of a drip/sprinkler system — NOT the adjective "side/lateral". Wrong renderings found: sw "taji" (crown). fr irrigation standard is "rampe". Keep one word per language and never alternate (it file mixed "laterale" and "manichetta").

ip.context: The trunk/supply pipe feeding the laterals in an irrigation system. Pairs with "lateral".
ip.translation_notes: Translate "main/mainline" as the trunk pipe, not the adjective "main". fr file left "main" untranslated ("Tronçons Main") — wrong.

ip.context: A segment of pipe or channel between two nodes/cross-sections. Table rows in Irrigation Pressure are reaches.
ip.translation_notes: Hydraulics noun, NOT "arrival/reaching" (ps "رسیدل" wrong), NOT "agent" (sw "mwakala" wrong), NOT "stripe" (km wrong). Bisection is the numerical root-finding method used to close the pressure loop in the Irrigation Pressure notes. (Wave 0, 2026-07-07, removed the former "right at the takeoff" and "draw off" wording from the English source.) Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): confirmed the single suite term per language — ar=قطاع (harmonized from a مقطع/قطاع split, مقطع left meaning cross-section) and ur=حصہ (harmonized from پہنچ in cs_ vs transliterated ریچ in ip_).

ip.context: Kinetic energy per unit weight, V²/2g — a height of water column.
ip.translation_notes: "Head" is a height of water column, never anatomical (cs "rychlostní hlava" wrong — use "rychlostní výška"). Task 109 stages 4-5 (2026-07-19): confirmed he=עומד מהירות (literal ראש 'head' calque removed) and sw=kimo cha kasi (Kichwa cha kasi calque removed).

ip.context: Head loss along the pipe due to wall friction (Darcy-Weisbach). Symbol h_f (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per label-normalization decision item 90, 2026-07-07). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure table column.
ip.translation_notes: Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): am 'ፍሪክሽን ኪሳራ' transliteration corrected to 'ግጭት ኪሳራ' (matches shipped mphl_friction_loss); same 'friction' fix applied across 5 keys.

ip.context: Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (coefficient k_m). Canonical merged concept for the former 'junction loss' (mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH LABEL: "Minor (local) loss" (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07). 'Minor ⇄ local' — a local/point loss at fittings, NOT a "smaller" loss; the '(local)' parenthetical fixes the mistranslation trap. Symbol h_m, coefficient k_m (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per the same decision). am ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 am re-translation): 'ጥቃቅን (አካባቢያዊ) ኪሳራ' (tiqaqin (akababiyawi) kisara) mirrors the English structure word-for-word — 'ጥቃቅን' (minor/small) followed by the parenthetical '(አካባቢያዊ)' (local, i.e. of a specific place/area) — so the same mistranslation-blocking device English uses (the '(local)' qualifier preventing a 'smaller loss' misreading) is preserved in Amharic rather than silently dropped. Replaces the prior am file's 'የማያያዣ ኪሳራ' (connector/joint loss), which named the physical fitting rather than the local/point-loss concept. km ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 km re-translation): 'ការបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋាន' (local-basis loss) reuses មូលដ្ឋាន ('local', already established suite-wide for this exact merged concept in ip_km's tooltip 'មេគុណបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋានសរុប' = 'total local-loss coefficient'), so category-3 now converges on the same word ip_ already uses rather than coining a second competing term. Deliberately avoids 'តូច' (small), sidestepping the minor⇄smaller mistranslation trap the English '(local)' parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the km file's prior mphl_junction_loss value 'ការបាត់បង់ junction' (untranslated English word left in place). ps ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 ps wave-3 re-translation): 'ځایی ضیاع' (local loss) uses ځایی (local/positional) + the established ps loss word ضیاع, following the majority pattern already set by ar/fa/es/fr/hr/id/it/ro/ru/sr/tr/uk/ur/zh — all of which render this concept as 'local loss' alone rather than translating 'minor' literally, since the '(local)' qualifier is the operative disambiguator, not 'minor'. Deliberately avoids a word for 'small/minor' (e.g. کوچنی) to sidestep the same minor⇄smaller trap the English parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the prior ps file's 'د جنکشن ضیاع' (junction loss — the pre-consolidation, pre-item-90 term) and fixes its symbol from capital H_m to lowercase h_m. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): de 'Minderverlust' (=lesser/reduced loss — the exact 'smaller loss' mistranslation the item-90 convention blocks) corrected to 'Örtlicher (Einzel-)Verlust' matching the labels.

ip.context: The total-head line (elevation + pressure head + velocity head) along a pipe or channel. Appears in Irrigation Pressure Method note.
ip.translation_notes: Use the established hydraulics term for the total-head line. NEVER calque word-by-word: es "Linea de Grado de Energia", fr "ligne d'energie grade", it "Linea di Grado Energia", ro "Linia Gradului Energetic", bg/uk "line of the energy class", cs "energy layer" are all wrong renderings found in shipped files. Task 109 stages 4-5 (2026-07-19): uk must be лінія енергії — the wrong-concept calque 'лінія питомої енергії' (specific-energy line, a distinct concept) was removed; cs 'energy layer' also corrected to grade line.
Hydraulics direction, never software "upgrade" (my file error). tr: memba = upstream, mansap = downstream — a tr file flipped these; pin them.

ip.context: Direction away from the supply, toward the outlet / last emitter.
ip.translation_notes: Never software "downgrade". ar: downstream = المصب / أسفل المجرى (a file used المنبعية = source-side, wrong).

rc.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
rc.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

rc.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
rc.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

rc.context: Angular rock placed to resist erosion on channel beds and banks. Appears in Manning Trapezoidal Channel and Rock Chute calculators.
rc.translation_notes: No direct single-word equivalent in most languages. Use the established local engineering term — this varies significantly by country. In Spanish, 'enrocado' (general) or 'escollera' (bank protection) are both used; lead with 'enrocado'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg: 'каменна облицовка' (stone lining), not 'каменна наброска'. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files. Task 97 (2026-07-13): tr's rock-chute (rc_) translation agent had actually diverged from this glossary value, using 'parça taşı' (rock fragment/piece) in 4 places instead of 'taş dolgu'; no native Turkish reviewer was available, so resolved by an AI (Opus) judgment call reasoning from suite convention — 'taş dolgu' ('stone fill', the established DSİ/TS term, cf. 'taş dolgu baraj' = rockfill dam) is correct for both the bulk-material and D50 particle-sizing senses, matching how es/fr/pt/ru all keep one bulk-material word rather than switching to a fragment/particle term for sizing contexts. Lang file corrected to 'taş dolgu' throughout; treat as our best-effort resolution, not pending native review (see CLAUDE.md 'Native review is real only when feedback actually lands'). Task 98 riprap audit (2026-07-13): found 6 of 26 languages (am, bn, he, hi, id, ur) had phonetically TRANSLITERATED the English word 'riprap' as a borrowed loanword instead of translating the concept — a real translation-quality defect, not a stylistic choice, concentrated in this specific bare/short-label term. English source renamed 'riprap' → 'rock lining' (see CLAUDE.md 'Write English source strings in Simple English') specifically because a transparent two-word English compound is much less likely to be transliterated than an opaque-looking jargon word; all 6 languages' rc_/mtc_ occurrences were corrected to real native terms in the same pass (each reusing that language's own already-successful translation pattern found elsewhere in its file). zh was separately found to use three inconsistent terms (块石/护坡/抛石) for this concept across different rc_ keys — not a transliteration issue, but the same 'pick one term and use it everywhere' defect — resolved by standardizing on 护坡 (slope protection/lining), which best matches the 'lining' sense and was already the plurality incumbent. The other 19 languages already had good native terms and needed no change — the concept translated fine, only the English word choice invited transliteration risk in weaker-resourced languages. Task 109 stage 2 (2026-07-19): ar/km/my/sw confirmed on real translated words — the phonetic-transliteration failure class (same as the 2026-07-13 rc_ audit) was checked and corrected where present.

rc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
rc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

rc.context: A steep rock-lined drop structure (also called a 'rock ramp') that conveys water rapidly down a slope in irrigation, drainage, or watershed management. Key concepts for translation: rock-lined, steep gradient, spillway or drop structure — translate the concept, not the English word 'chute'. The rock riprap matrix dissipates energy and resists erosion. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson) and Robinson Rock Chute calculators.
rc.translation_notes: CRITICAL: 'Robinson' is the surname of K.M. Robinson, co-author of Robinson, Rice & Kadavy (1998) — it is a proper noun and must NEVER be translated or modified in any language. Translate only 'Rock Chute'. Concept to translate: 'rock-lined steep channel' or 'rock-lined spillway' — the drop/descent nature must be conveyed; a generic 'rock channel' is insufficient. CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 establishes that the French word 'chute' means 'fall' (elevation difference) — it cannot name this structure. Use 'coursier en enrochement' (coursier = steep channel structure; enrochement = riprap). Spanish: USDA uses 'bajante de rocado' — 'bajante' (from bajar = to descend) correctly conveys the drop-structure nature; 'de rocado' = rock-lined. Russian: 'каменный быстроток' ('быстроток' = fast-flow/steep channel). Portuguese: changed from 'calha' (generic trough) to 'rampa em enrocamento' (rampa = ramp/slope, enrocamento = riprap) to convey steep character. Serbian: changed from 'жлеб' (gutter/trough) to 'брзоток' (fast-flow structure), consistent with ru/uk pattern. Bengali: changed from borrowed 'চ্যুট' (conveys nothing) to 'পাথর-আবৃত খাড়া নালা' (rock-lined steep channel). Persian: changed from generic 'آبراه سنگی' (stone waterway) to 'آبراه تند سنگچین' (تند = steep/swift, سنگچین = stone-laid/riprap). Pashto: added 'تند' (steep/swift) to original. Khmer: changed 'ចំហ' (open) to 'ជម្រាល' (sloped/inclined). NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: am (ምቀጫ meaning uncertain), my (ထောင် may not clearly convey steep to all readers), de (Steinschütte is standard engineering term but doesn't explicitly say 'steep channel'). Turkish: changed to 'taş düşü' — 'düşü' is the established Turkish hydraulics term for a drop/chute structure (2026-07 audit; previous 'taş eğimli kanal' was descriptive but nonstandard). Spanish: NEEDS HUMAN VERIFICATION — 'bajante de rocado' claims a USDA source but 'rocado' is not standard Spanish ('enrocado' is); verify the USDA document or switch to 'bajante de enrocado'. 2026-07 reconciliation: fr/ro/ru/uk lang files updated to match this entry. NOT reconciled pending human review of the GLOSSARY side: hr 'kameni skluz' (consider 'kameni brzotok', parallel to sr/ru), bg 'каменна бързина' (consider 'каменен бързоток'), de 'Steinschütte' vs shipped 'Steingerinne' (both defensible - pick one). RESOLVED bg: native Bulgarian engineer confirmed 'каменен бързоток' (2026-07); lang file updated. Task 98 (2026-07-13): English source renamed 'Rock Chute' → 'Steep Channel' throughout the rc_ prefix (see CLAUDE.md 'Write English source strings in Simple English') — 'chute' itself is jargon-shaped English that some languages transliterated rather than translated. The earlier Bengali fix noted above only reached the calculator's title-level strings (rc_main_menu/rc_main_desc); a full-file grep found 'চ্যুট' still transliterated in 7 more rc_ body keys (rc_S0, rc_qt, rc_n_chute, rc_pond_ok_tip, rc_pond_warn_tip, rc_notes_2_def, rc_notes_3_def, rc_notes_7_def) — fixed 2026-07-13 to match the title's 'খাড়া নালা'. Hindi and Urdu had the same bare-transliteration defect suite-wide ('चूट'/'چوٹ') despite their titles being fine in some cases — fixed to 'तीव्र ढाल चैनल' (hi) and 'کھڑی نالی' (ur), applied consistently across every rc_ occurrence. Lesson: a healthy title-level translation does not guarantee the same concept was translated (vs. transliterated) in every short body label — check the whole file, not just the title strings, when auditing a jargon term.

rc.context: A steep open channel or drop structure for conveying water rapidly down a slope. Distinct from a gentle-slope irrigation canal. Per ec_lang_intent guidance: translate as 'steep channel' or 'spillway' — not as the word 'chute' borrowed into another language. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson), Manning Trapezoidal Channel, and related drop-structure calculators.
rc.translation_notes: CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 defines the English word 'fall' (elevation difference) as French 'chute', Spanish 'caída', and Russian 'падение'. The same pattern holds in all three WMO languages: the word for 'fall' (elevation difference) is NOT available for this hydraulic structure. 'Coursier' is the correct French term for the structure. Spanish: 'canal rápido'. Russian: 'быстроток' (the steep channel structure — distinct from 'падение' which means elevation fall). Chinese: '陡槽'. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 sr audit found the glossary's own value (брзотек) was the stem-drift error; corrected to брзоток, consistent with ru/uk pattern and rc_ identity strings. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 ps audit aligned to the file's own established identity-string term (تند اوبو لار) over a divergent glossary spelling, for cross-key consistency within category 5.

rc.context: Flow rate per unit width of channel (Q/B), in m²/s or ft²/s. The primary design input for the Robinson rock chute method. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
rc.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic engineering term. 'Unit' here means 'per unit channel width' — not related to measurement units. Spanish: 'caudal unitario'. French: 'débit unitaire'. German: 'spezifischer Abfluss'. Russian: 'удельный расход'. Chinese: '单宽流量'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg hydraulics uses 'водно количество' for discharge, not 'дебит'.

rc.context: The particle size at which 50% of the rock is finer by weight. The primary output of the Robinson rock chute method. Also used in Manning Trapezoidal Channel riprap sizing. The symbol D50 is universal — translate only the descriptive label.
rc.translation_notes: D50 (or D₅₀) is a universal engineering symbol — do not translate it. Translate only the label 'median rock size' or 'median particle size'. Most languages express this as 'median diameter'. Do not use 'average' (average ≠ median statistically). Spanish: 'tamaño mediano de roca'. French: 'taille médiane des rochers'. Chinese: '中值粒径'. **2026-07-13 cross-language research pass (item 44):** researched whether 'average/mean'-register wording (found in several languages' initial translations) is a real engineering error or defensible practice-register, using web research into each language's actual geotechnical/sedimentology literature. Confirmed real errors, corrected in both the lang files and this glossary: de ('mittlere'→'mediane'/'medianer', citing German BAW government sedimentology usage), cs ('střední'→'mediánová', citing Charles University hydraulics course), ru ('средний'→'медианный' for mi_d50in; rc_D50 already correct), tr ('orta'→'ortanca', matching the term already correct in rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), fa ('متوسط'→'میانه', citing Persian percentile-based technical definitions), ur ('اوسط'/'درمیانی'/'درمیانہ'→'وسیط', mirroring Arabic's وسيط/متوسط distinction), sr ('средња'→'медијанска', matching mi_d50in which already used 'Медијана'). Found already correct in the lang files (glossary was simply stale, not the file — see item 42): bg ('медианен размер', confirmed live in mi_d50in/rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), uk ('медіанний розмір'), hr ('medijalna veličina', an adjective form of medijan/medijana), ro ('dimensiunea mediană'). One language, am (Amharic), was researched and found to have no distinct circulating median-vs-average term at all — even Amharic dictionaries gloss 'median' as 'መካከለኛ' (same word used for 'middle/average') — so 'የድንጋይ መካከለኛ መጠን' was left unchanged; there's no more-correct term available in practice.

rc.context: The spread or uniformity of rock particle sizes. In the Robinson method, gradation is expressed as SD = D84.1/D50. Uniform rock ≈ 1.25; Robinson valid range 1.15–1.47. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
rc.translation_notes: Use the geotechnical/hydraulic engineering term for grain size distribution or grading. Do not translate as 'grade' (implies quality). The symbol 'SD' and ratio notation D84.1/D50 are universal. Spanish/Portuguese: 'granulometría'/'granulometria'. French: 'granulométrie'. Russian/Bulgarian/Serbian: 'гранулометрический состав'. Chinese: '级配'. bg: native engineer confirmed 2026-07-06 the standard term for the D84.1/D50 gradation SD label is 'Коефициент на градация' (superseding the earlier 'коефициент на едрозърнестост' proposal and the alternative 'коефициент на разнозърненост'); applied in rc_SD/rc_SD_check. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files.

rc.context: The fraction of the rock layer volume that is void space (air + water). Default 0.45 for angular crushed rock. Determines how much flow passes through the rock mantle versus over the surface. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator. Distinct from Manning's n (roughness coefficient) — do not confuse the two.
rc.translation_notes: Standard hydraulic/geotechnical term with cognates in most European languages. Always distinguish from Manning 'n' in context — they appear in the same calculator.

rc.context: Dimensionless ratio of a material's density to the density of water (≈2.65 for crushed granite/basalt; Robinson valid range 2.54–2.82). Appears in Rock Chute Design and Manning Trapezoidal Channel. The English source keeps "specific gravity" — the standard English term and the one Robinson's paper uses (rc_ cites it). We deliberately do NOT swap it for "relative density" even though that reads as more modern: per Tom's principle (2026-07-20) we defer to each language's own dominant standard term rather than judging terminology.
rc.translation_notes: [2026-07-20 RESOLUTION — Tom's principle: 'we are not the judges of terminology, culture is.'] Use each language's dominant, culturally-standard term for this dimensionless concept, whatever its literal composition. A weight-flavored STANDARD term is CORRECT, not an error to be reformed toward 'relative density': tr 'özgül ağırlık', he 'משקל סגולי' (standard Hebrew physics-curriculum term), sr 'специфична тежина', ps 'ځانګړی ثقل' are the established local standards and stay. The ONLY hard rule is physical — the value is a dimensionless ratio and never carries units. hr RESOLVED to 'relativna gustoća', the dominant modern Croatian standard (gustoća = density), matching the shipped file; the glossary was the stale side. sw 'uzito maalum' is NOT an auto-defect: if it is the standard Swahili term for the concept used dimensionlessly (parallel to Turkish özgül ağırlık), it is correct — confirm it is the Swahili standard, do not replace it with a coined 'relative density' calque. This supersedes the earlier 'weight-word exception' framing, which wrongly implied 'relative density' was the target to push. [2026-07-21 assessment] Two more glossary values were stale vs. their shipped, internally-consistent files (same class as hr): sr updated 'специфична тежина'→'релативна густина' and it 'peso specifico relativo'→'densità relativa' to match each file's actual standard usage; no lang-file change needed. (Historical: de 'spezifisches Gewicht'→'relative Dichte' and ru 'удельный вес'→'относительная плотность' were corrected in the 2026-07-08 category-1 QA — those were genuine non-standard-in-context values, not the same as a language whose actual standard is weight-flavored.) [2026-07-21 Task 131 tip sprint] 'Density relative to water' definitional tip now ships in all 26 languages on mtc_sgrock/rc_sg. NEW cross-key LABEL drift found (distinct from the glossary-vs-file staleness above): within a single language the two calculators disagree on the SG term — mtc_sgrock uses a weight-flavored label while rc_sg uses a relative-density-flavored one — in pt (Gravidade específica vs Densidade relativa), uk (Питома вага vs Відносна густина), ar (الكثافة النوعية vs الكثافة النسبية), fa (وزن مخصوص نسبی vs چگالی نسبی); sr already noted.
